fields.meta_title: Guest List Form Builder With Caps and Plus-Ones | Emergent
fields.meta_description: Build a guest list form that caps names per host, takes plus-ones, closes at a cutoff, and sends the final list to the door. Free to start.
fields.h1: Build a Guest List Form the Door Can Work From
fields.hero_description: Build a guest list form that caps each host's names, closes at a set time, and saves every guest to a database you own.
fields.features_heading: What the Door Needs Before the First Guest
fields.features_subheading: A guest list form sets who can add names and when the list closes. The door ends up with one final list, sorted and counted.
fields.feature_1:
A name limit on every host's link

Give each promoter or host their own link with a set number of names. The form counts what each one has added and stops taking names from that link once the limit is reached.
fields.feature_2:
Plus-ones listed by name, not as +1

Let each guest add one companion by name instead of a blank +1. Both names go on the list, both count toward the event's capacity, and the door sees who arrived with whom.
fields.feature_3:
A waitlist that opens when the list fills

When the list reaches capacity, new sign-ups land on a waitlist in the order they arrived. Remove a guest from the list and the first waitlisted name takes the open spot.
fields.feature_4:
A cutoff kept to the minute

Set the time the list closes, such as 8 pm on the night. After that the form shows a closed message, and the door manager gets the final list by email, sorted by last name.
fields.feature_5:
A door view that marks guests arrived

Open the list on a tablet at the door, search a last name, and tap once to mark the guest arrived. The count of guests inside updates as staff work through the line outside.
fields.feature_6:
Code that leaves with you

On paid plans, export the full code to your GitHub repository. Host the guest list on your own servers and keep its table beside the rest of your event and venue systems.

fields.usecase_heading: Who Adds the Names, and Who Reads Them
fields.tab_content_1:
One promoter link, 25 names and no 26th

Cassius Ravensworth promotes Saturday nights at the Lantern Room, and his link takes up to 25 names. He adds his 25th guest at 7:40 pm, and the form stops taking names from him. The list closes for every promoter at 8 pm. Door manager Imelda Duquesne then gets an email with all 79 names, sorted by last name.
fields.tab_content_2:
When a plus-one fills spot 60, the next guest waits

Corisande Mott caps her 40th birthday at 60 people, plus-ones included. Leopold Tamsworth adds his name and his partner, Hollis Pembrey, which brings the list to 60. Delphine Arkwright signs up that evening and lands first on the waitlist. If anyone drops out, her name moves onto the list.
fields.tab_content_3:
All 112 names reach security by 6 pm

Kestrelmoor Robotics hosts a launch night in its office lobby. Employees add each guest with the name on their photo ID, their company, and their own name as host. The list closes at 6 pm the day before, and security lead Bartholomew Nkemelu gets all 112 names by email.
fields.tab_content_4:
On the door tablet, 87 of 140 are in

The Tidewell Gallery opening has 140 names on its list. At the door, Marguerite Ostrander searches Aurelio Stanhope by last name and taps once to mark him arrived. The live count moves to 87 of 140. The curator watches the same count on her phone and starts the talk when the room fills.

fields.howto_title: How to Create a Guest List Form
fields.howto_description: Seven steps to a guest list form that limits who adds names, closes on time, and hands the door a list to check off.
fields.howto_step_2_title: 02 Set the limits before the link goes out
fields.howto_step_3_title: 03 Ask only for what the door checks
fields.howto_step_1_des: Write down who is allowed to add names: the guests themselves, hosts, promoters, or employees. A birthday party can let guests sign up directly, while a club hands each promoter a link. That choice decides whether the form needs a host field.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Pick a number for each host and a capacity for the whole event, and decide whether plus-ones count toward it. Settle what happens at the limit, a waitlist or a closed message, before anyone sees the form.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Ask for first and last names in separate fields so the list sorts cleanly. Add a plus-one name, a company, or a host only when someone at the door will read it. Every extra field slows down the person filling it in.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Pick a cutoff the door can live with, such as two hours before doors open, or the evening before for a building lobby. Decide who gets the final list at that moment and in what order it arrives.
fields.howto_step_5_des: Put the people, limits, fields, and cutoff into one prompt. Emergent builds the guest list form, the database behind it, and a door view for staff. Change a limit or a field later by asking in plain English.
fields.howto_step_6_des: Open the door view on a tablet and search a few names to see how quickly they come up. Give a second staff member the link if the line will be long, since both screens show the same arrivals count.
fields.howto_step_7_title: 07 Sign up as a fake guest
fields.howto_step_7_des: Run a test entry through every link, including once past the limit and once after the cutoff. Check that the waitlist catches the extra name and that the final list email reaches the right inbox.

faq_plan.q: What is a guest list form?
faq_plan.a: A guest list form collects the names of the people allowed into an event, entered by the guests themselves or by the hosts who invite them. Each entry becomes one row on a single list, which staff at the door use to admit people and count arrivals.

faq_plan.q: How do I create a guest list form?
faq_plan.a: Decide who adds names, how many each person may add, and when the list closes. Put those limits and the fields you need into one prompt to Emergent's AI form builder. You get a link to share, a table holding every name, and a screen the door works from.

faq_plan.q: What should a guest list form ask for?
faq_plan.a: Ask for the guest's first and last name in separate fields, plus the host who added them when more than one person is adding names. Add an email field if guests should get a confirmation that their name is on the list. Leave out anything nobody at the door will read on the night.

faq_plan.q: Is a guest list form the same as an RSVP?
faq_plan.a: No. A guest list form records who is allowed in, while an RSVP records an invited person's reply. Names go on a guest list until a limit or a cutoff, and the door checks against it. An RSVP asks people already invited whether they are coming and can collect meal choices for a household. For a wedding, where every reply feeds the seating chart, build a wedding rsvp form instead.

faq_plan.q: How many names should each promoter get on a guest list form?
faq_plan.a: Start from the room's capacity and work backward. Hold back a block for walk-ins and the venue's own guests, then split the rest, such as 4 promoters at 25 names each for a 150-person room with 50 held back. Raise a promoter's number next time if 20 of their 25 names checked in. Emergent's forms have no response caps, so the only limits are the ones you set.

faq_plan.q: Can a host add names after a guest list form closes?
faq_plan.a: Yes, if the form gives the host a separate way in. Keep the shared link closed at the cutoff and give the door manager a late-add field. Each name added there carries a late tag, so the final count shows who came in after the list closed.

faq_plan.q: Should a guest list form collect card details?
faq_plan.a: No. Keep a guest list to names and the details the door reads. When a table or a private room needs a card on file, collect it on a separate credit card authorization form and match the two by the guest's name.

faq_plan.q: Can door staff add walk-ins to a guest list form?
faq_plan.a: Yes, when the door view includes a walk-in button. Staff type the guest's name, it joins the list already marked arrived, and it carries a walk-in tag. The arrivals count stays right, and the host sees afterward who came without being listed. Emergent adds that button when you ask for it in a prompt, even after the list is live.

faq_plan.q: What happens when two hosts add the same guest to a guest list form?
faq_plan.a: The app can flag the second entry when a first and last name already on the list come in again, and show which host added that guest first. You decide whether the form refuses the repeat or keeps both and marks them for the door manager. The match runs on the name as typed: a nickname such as Bill for William still gets through.

faq_plan.q: Can a gym use a guest list form for a bring-a-friend class?
faq_plan.a: Yes. Give each member a link that adds one friend by name to a class with a set number of spots, and close it the night before. The front desk checks friends in from that list. A friend who signs up afterward goes through the gym's own intake, such as a fitness assessment form, before training starts.
